title: arXiv Physics — 2 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this is an inferred evidence-weighted ranking with limited citation evidence for papers in the same announcement batch, not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons in signatures with one prompt muon and a secondary vertex formed by two non-prompt muons in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 and 13.6 TeV
sections.abstract: CMS searches for heavy neutral leptons in W-boson decays using one prompt and two displaced muons in 13 and 13.6 TeV proton collisions; it finds no excess and sets mixing limits under the Majorana hypothesis.
sections.claimed_result: CMS reports no significant deviation from its control-sample background prediction and sets 95% confidence-level Majorana-HNL mixing limits for masses 1–5 GeV, with improved sensitivity at 2.5–4.2 GeV.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; CMS LHC proton-proton data totaling 138 fb-1 at 13 TeV and 34.6 fb-1 at 13.6 TeV.
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted exclusion assumes Majorana HNLs; background transfer-factor uncertainties are sizable, especially for the 2022 sample.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured in Antonio Marrone’s 2 November arXiv digest; a CMS-collaboration search combines 2016–2018 and 2022 data and targets a long-lifetime, low-mass region with muon-system displaced vertices.

sections.title: Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
sections.abstract: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy observes a Dirac gap in monolayer graphene only during circularly polarized driving, which the authors associate with a light-induced Haldane mass using Floquet theory.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the Dirac gap appears synchronously with the optical field and only under circular polarization; calculations associate it with dynamical time-reversal-symmetry breaking and Floquet Chern topology.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TrARPES), interpreted with Floquet electronic-structure calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The directly measured quantity is the transient spectral gap; the Berry curvature and Chern characterization are inferred from Floquet calculations, and the gap uncertainty includes a momentum-window systematic.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports a direct spectroscopic signature under circular, but not other, optical driving and combines time-resolved measurements with Floquet calculations; the full text describes its gap extraction and systematic estimate.

sections.title: Phenomenological Chiral Effective Field Theory for Neutrino Event Generators
sections.abstract: The authors build a gauge-invariant chiral effective-field-theory model for single-pion production and automate its path from Lagrangian to event generation, validating it against photoproduction and existing neutrino and electron-scattering data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors present a systematically extendable resonance-region model with consistent spin-3/2 and gauge-invariant couplings, implemented from Lagrangian to simulated events.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; phenomenological chiral EFT implemented with FeynRules, UFO 2.0, and Sherpa and compared with existing scattering data.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that nuclear single-pion datasets disagree in normalization beyond quoted uncertainties and no event generator describes them all together; some low-statistics comparison data also have unassessed systematics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured in the 2 November arXiv digest; the work supplies an automated FeynRules/UFO/Sherpa pipeline and compares with multiple bubble-chamber, MINERvA, T2K, MicroBooNE, MiniBooNE, and electron-carbon datasets.

sections.title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
sections.abstract: Broadband pulse-profile modeling of PSR J0437−4715 using NICER and other observatories yields updated mass and radius estimates, which the authors combine with other pulsar measurements to constrain the dense-matter equation of state.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report M=1.377(+0.038/-0.034) solar masses and equatorial radius 11.35(+0.40/-0.39) km (68% credible intervals); combined with other pulsars, their inference excludes EOS models predicting radii above 12 km for all neutron-star masses at the 68% level.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; Bayesian pulse-profile modeling of NICER, XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, and HST data with radio-timing priors.
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred radius depends on the hot-spot, warm-surface, and non-thermal emission models and on informative mass, distance, and inclination priors; the authors discuss sensitivity to emission-model choices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The inference combines 2.56 Ms of NICER data with XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, Hubble far-UV observations, and radio-timing priors, producing a tightly stated mass-radius result with direct EOS relevance.

sections.title: The Yottascale at Tera-Z: Petascale SUSY?
sections.abstract: The authors examine how future Tera-Z gauge-coupling precision and proton-decay constraints affect minimal supersymmetric SU(5), finding markedly different implications at two and three loops.
sections.claimed_result: In the authors’ nearly degenerate SUSY-spectrum scenario, the two-loop analysis points to a SUSY scale near 1 PeV, while the three-loop analysis appears to exclude the minimal model because the color-triplet Higgs mass is fixed by infrared parameters at one-loop GUT-threshold order.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; renormalization-group and threshold calculations using present data and projected Tera-Z and proton-decay constraints.
sections.unique_caveat: These are conditional model projections, not measurements; conclusions depend on minimal SU(5), the assumed spectrum, and treatment of higher-loop and GUT-threshold corrections.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured in the 2 November arXiv digest; it connects projected FCC-ee/Tera-Z precision to GUT-scale running and exposes a sharp loop-order dependence in a defined minimal-SU(5) scenario.

sections.title: Magnetic scattering experiments with an ultrashort pulsed soft X-ray source using iLGADs
sections.abstract: The authors test iLGAD hybrid-pixel detectors with a laser-driven soft X-ray source and demonstrate time-synchronized magnetic small-angle X-ray scattering of a FeGd heterostructure, with higher photon-detection efficiency than a standard silicon sensor in the comparison.
sections.claimed_result: In the reported comparison, iLGAD sensors provide higher photon-detection efficiency and sensitivity than standard silicon sensors, and the experiment probes magnetic domains in FeGd; the abstract also reports single-photon detection at 400 eV with SNR above 5 and quantum efficiency above 85% at 250 eV.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; laser-driven soft X-ray measurements with iLGADs bump-bonded to MÖNCH readout chips, including a magnetic SAXS test.
sections.unique_caveat: The scattering demonstration is a detector/source test on a FeGd heterostructure over a limited energy range, not a broad survey of detector performance across facilities or samples.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantitative detector performance is tied to a completed magnetic-scattering demonstration using few-picosecond X-ray pulses, rather than only a proposed sensor concept.

sections.title: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
sections.abstract: A two-flavor calculation in an equal-mass Majumdar–Papapetrou dihole spacetime finds that interference between neutrino paths can introduce sensitivity to individual masses and mass ordering for nonmaximal mixing.
sections.claimed_result: Within the null approximation and symmetry-plane setup, the authors find path interference can make transition probabilities depend on individual neutrino masses and ordering, beyond the usual mass-squared-difference dependence for nonmaximal mixing.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; leading-order phase calculation and numerical geodesic integrals in an idealized two-black-hole geometry.
sections.unique_caveat: The result depends on an equal-mass static dihole, a null-propagation approximation, two flavors, and selected source-detector paths; it is not a prediction for an observed astrophysical neutrino signal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured in the 2 November arXiv digest and cross-listed between gravitation and particle phenomenology; it makes a concrete, testable-in-principle prediction about how multiple lensed trajectories alter the oscillation phase.

sections.title: A first look at strange-quark polarization in top-quark decays with CMS Open Data
sections.abstract: Using 16.39 fb-1 of public CMS data, the author makes a first end-to-end measurement of Lambda-baryon polarization in strange jets from semileptonic top-pair events; the limited-precision result is consistent with zero and with the LEP-inferred transfer.
sections.claimed_result: The paper reports longitudinal Lambda polarization P_parallel=+0.04±0.45 (stat)±0.06 (syst) for the z>0.3 region, consistent with zero and with the transfer inferred from LEP but not precise enough to test it.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 2016 CMS Open Data from 13 TeV proton collisions, 16.39 fb-1, in semileptonic ttbar events.
sections.unique_caveat: Statistical uncertainty dominates and the result cannot yet resolve the polarization-transfer question; acceptance correction, backgrounds, and baryon/antibaryon effects need stronger control.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A first realization of strange-quark polarimetry on open collider data, with a specified public dataset and a concrete analysis chain; the paper also identifies what higher-statistics Run-2/Run-3 measurements would need to control.

sections.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
sections.abstract: DMRG simulations of a four-leg chiral-fermion ladder find quantized charge pumping across gapless and gapped boundary phases, while the spatial charge distribution changes; the authors propose an analogy to topological leptogenesis.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find an intermediate symmetric-mass-generation edge phase that is fully gapped, yet charge pumped per flux quantum remains quantized across all three boundary phases; the proposed leptogenesis connection is an analogy, not a cosmological result.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; density-matrix renormalization-group simulations of a four-leg quasi-(2+1)-dimensional 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral-fermion model.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is from a finite-width lattice simulation; the proposed link to Standard Model leptogenesis is conceptual and does not establish a mechanism in the early universe.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured in the 2 November digest and cross-listed between strongly correlated matter and quantum physics; the simulations compare weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling boundary regimes and report a common quantized pumped charge.

sections.title: First Light with the Dark100 Array of PANOSETI Telescopes at Palomar Observatory
sections.abstract: This status report describes the first phase of the seven-telescope Dark100/PANOSETI array for ultra-high-energy gamma-ray observations and ultra-heavy dark-matter searches, with more than 100 hours of observations collected during commissioning.
sections.claimed_result: The authors describe the first four installed telescopes, over 100 hours of three-telescope data on sources including the Crab Nebula and Markarian 421, and the planned completion of a seven-telescope array.
sections.evidence_type: Observational and instrumentation; commissioning observations and array-performance simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a source or dark-matter detection; the array is incomplete, and the abstract reports status rather than a final gamma-ray measurement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports an instrument entering operation, concrete observing time on established targets, and an expansion from optical-transient instrumentation into UHE gamma-ray astronomy; it is an isolated instrumentation/status signal in this selection.
